subtasks.description: Vocabulary of six tokens t0..t5 with logits z = [2.0, 1.0, 0.5, 0.2, -1.0, -3.0]. Implement in NumPy a numerically stable temperature softmax p_i = exp((z_i - max(z))/T) / sum_j exp((z_j - max(z))/T) (subtracting the max before dividing by T is a valid stable formulation; any equivalent stable implementation is acceptable). Compute the distribution for T = 0.5, T = 1 and T = 2, and the Shannon entropy in bits (log base 2) of each distribution. Present the three distributions and the three entropies in a single table (e.g. a pandas DataFrame) with all values rounded to 4 decimals. Print/display the table so it is visible in the executed notebook.
criteria: Uses the exact logits [2.0, 1.0, 0.5, 0.2, -1.0, -3.0] for tokens t0..t5
Softmax is numerically stable (handles large/small logits without overflow, e.g. subtracting the max logit)
Computes distributions for T = 0.5, 1 and 2; each row sums to 1
Entropies are computed in bits (log base 2)
Shows one table with the three distributions and three entropies, all figures with 4 decimals
Values are computed in the notebook, not hardcoded

subtasks.description: Recompute (in this script, independently) the softmax distribution at T = 1 from the logits z = [2.0, 1.0, 0.5, 0.2, -1.0, -3.0] for tokens t0..t5, using the same numerically stable implementation as Part 1. Apply nucleus (top-p) sampling with p = 0.9: sort the tokens by probability in descending order, keep the minimal set of tokens whose cumulative probability reaches or exceeds 0.9, and renormalize their probabilities to sum to 1. Report which tokens survive and the renormalized distribution (4 decimals), plus the cumulative probabilities used to decide the cut.
criteria: Recomputes the T = 1 softmax from the same logits (does not rely on files from Part 1)
Sorts tokens by descending probability and keeps the minimal set with cumulative probability >= 0.9
Reports explicitly which tokens survive the top-p cut
Reports the renormalized distribution over surviving tokens (4 decimals), summing to 1
Shows the cumulative probabilities that justify the cut

subtasks.description: Recompute (in this script, independently) the renormalized top-p distribution: stable softmax at T = 1 over logits z = [2.0, 1.0, 0.5, 0.2, -1.0, -3.0] for tokens t0..t5, then top-p with p = 0.9 (sort descending, minimal set with cumulative probability >= 0.9, renormalize). Draw 10,000 samples from this renormalized distribution using numpy.random.default_rng(0). Compute the observed empirical frequencies of each surviving token. Produce a grouped bar chart comparing observed frequencies vs theoretical (renormalized) probabilities per token, with axis labels, a legend and token names on the x-axis. Compute the KL divergence D_KL(empirical || theoretical) in bits (log base 2) using only the surviving tokens, and report its value (4 decimals).
criteria: Recomputes the renormalized top-p distribution from the same logits and parameters (T = 1, p = 0.9)
Uses numpy.random.default_rng(0) and exactly 10,000 samples
Produces a bar chart comparing observed frequencies with theoretical probabilities, with labels and legend
Computes KL divergence in bits (log base 2) of the empirical distribution relative to the theoretical one and reports it with 4 decimals
Chart is generated in the notebook and displayed

subtasks.description: Conceptual question, answered in prose in a Markdown cell. Explain what happens to the output distribution as T → 0 and as T → ∞, and why T → 0 is equivalent to greedy decoding. Use as evidence the entropies computed in Part 1 for T = 0.5, 1 and 2 (logits z = [2.0, 1.0, 0.5, 0.2, -1.0, -3.0]): as T decreases the distribution concentrates on the argmax token and entropy falls toward 0 (deterministic, greedy choice); as T grows the distribution flattens toward uniform over the six tokens and entropy grows toward log2(6) ≈ 2.585 bits. Cite the actual entropy values from Part 1 in the explanation.
criteria: Explains the T → 0 limit: distribution concentrates on the token with the highest logit, entropy tends to 0
Explains the T → ∞ limit: distribution tends to uniform over the 6 tokens, entropy tends to log2(6) ≈ 2.585 bits
Justifies why T → 0 equals greedy decoding (argmax token takes probability ~1)
Cites the entropy values from Part 1 as evidence
Written as clear prose in a Markdown cell, no code required
